source: Rye Daze Song Laboratory — Collection 02, 22 October 2026

labs.title: Two Worlds Collide
labs.inspiration: Hiatus Kaiyote × The Comet Is Coming × Flying Lotus · 56 bars
labs.idea: Start with a loose, organic jazz-funk groove. Gradually infiltrate it with electronic elements until the song becomes something completely different.
labs.challenge: Make the transformation feel intentional. Which elements should change gradually, and which should arrive as a complete surprise?

bars.instruction: Create a drum groove with a loose, human feel. Add a syncopated bassline and short, rhythmic chord stabs using your pads.
Introduce a melodic hook. Add a second percussion layer that plays around the main drum rhythm.
Create an electronic drum pattern with a noticeably different rhythmic character. Introduce tiny fragments of it between the original drum hits.
Gradually remove the organic drums. Bring in a new synth texture. In bars 31–32, remove the bass and let a sound effect or processed melodic fragment carry you into the next section.
Introduce the full electronic drum pattern, a new bassline and a different approach to the chord rhythm. Reintroduce fragments of your original melody, perhaps chopped or processed.
Bring back the original bassline beneath the electronic drums. Add some of the earlier percussion. Experiment with combining the two rhythmic identities.
Create a final hybrid groove. Strip away its layers over the last four bars until one recognisable element remains.

labs.title: The False Beginning
labs.inspiration: King Krule × Connan Mockasin × BADBADNOTGOOD · 40 bars
labs.idea: Convince the listener that they've understood your song, then reveal something completely unexpected.
labs.challenge: Practise an abrupt transition that still feels musically connected. Use at least one recognisable element to bridge the two sections.

bars.instruction: Introduce a warm chord progression, simple bassline and steady drum groove. Add a small melodic motif. Make it feel like a perfectly plausible opening.
Develop the groove with a countermelody or additional percussion. Let the listener settle into it.
Start creating tension. Remove a familiar element, change the bass rhythm and introduce a strange background sound.
Completely disrupt the arrangement. Cut the drums, distort or filter the chords, and allow an unfamiliar rhythmic fragment to emerge.
Launch into a substantially different groove. Give the bass a new role and introduce a new melodic idea.
Reintroduce the melody from the opening, but place it inside this new groove. Finish with a deliberate ending rather than a fade.

labs.title: The Dub Tunnel
labs.inspiration: King Tubby × Floating Points × Nubiyan Twist · 48 bars
labs.idea: Use effects, space and subtraction to transform a groove without writing an entirely new song.
labs.challenge: Make a sparse section just as interesting as the full arrangement. The effects aren't decoration — they're participating in the composition.

bars.instruction: Build a rhythm section with bass, drums and spacious chord stabs.
Introduce a short melody or rhythmic hook. Add a subtle atmospheric texture.
Start removing drum elements. Send selected chord stabs or melodic fragments into delays. Create moments where the echoes answer the instruments.
Strip the arrangement down to bass, sparse percussion and echoes. Automate filters and reverbs so the texture keeps evolving.
Introduce a new rhythmic variation. Change the timing or placement of the chord stabs while maintaining the original harmonic identity.
Restore the full groove. Bring the original hook back, then finish by letting one delayed fragment decay into silence.

labs.title: The Bassline Changes Everything
labs.idea: Make the bassline the principal driver of your arrangement. Everything else responds to it.
labs.challenge: Learn how much musical development you can create by changing the bass part while keeping other elements recognisable.

bars.instruction: Start with bass and percussion only. Create a bassline with a recognisable rhythmic personality.
Introduce your chord pads. Let the chords interact rhythmically with the bass rather than simply holding sustained notes.
Add a melodic hook. In the final two bars, change the ending of your bass phrase to announce a transition.
Create a contrasting bassline using a different register, rhythm or articulation. Keep some of the existing chords or melody so the listener can hear the difference.
Change the drum groove to support the new bassline. Introduce a melodic variation.
Return to the original bassline but retain the newer drum rhythm. Experiment with a call-and-response ending between bass and melody.

labs.title: The Rhythmic Relay
labs.inspiration: Sons of Kemet × Orchestra Baobab × broken beat · 56 bars
labs.idea: A repeating rhythmic idea travels between instruments, changing character as it goes.
labs.challenge: Develop continuity between sections without depending on an unchanged chord progression or repeating eight-bar loop.

bars.instruction: Create a percussion groove using two or three contrasting sounds. Give one sound a distinctive repeating rhythmic phrase.
Add drums and bass. Introduce a chord part that leaves space for the percussion.
Transfer the rhythmic phrase from percussion to short chord stabs. Alter or mute the original percussion part so you're not merely doubling it.
Introduce a melody that echoes the rhythmic phrase. Change the drum accents to support the new melodic emphasis.
Remove the chord rhythm. Transfer the phrase into the bassline, and create a contrasting section with a sparser drum groove.
Build a call-and-response between bass, percussion and melody. Leave gaps rather than allowing every part to play simultaneously.
Return to the first groove. Choose one version of the rhythmic phrase to dominate the final section, then create an ending around it.

labs.title: The Ghost in the Machine
labs.inspiration: Flying Lotus × Machinedrum × psychedelic jazz · 40 bars
labs.idea: Create an entire song where seemingly insignificant background sounds gradually reveal a hidden musical structure. This one is particularly inspired by your experiments with XLN XO.
labs.challenge: Turn sound design into composition. Make the textures meaningful to the song's structure, not simply atmospheric embellishments.

bars.instruction: Create an XO pattern using glitches, mechanical noises, vinyl sounds or field recordings instead of normal drums. Add atmospheric chord pads.
Introduce conventional drums and a bassline. Keep the XO pattern underneath, acting as an unusual percussion layer.
Add a short melodic phrase. Experiment with processing one or two notes into unusual textures.
Remove the main drums. Rearrange your XO pattern so different sounds now emphasise the rhythm.
Introduce a contrasting bassline and rhythmic chord part. Repurpose a sound from your original XO pattern as an obvious rhythmic hook.
Gradually merge elements of the original groove with the contrasting section.
Remove the conventional instruments, leaving only the texture pattern. Finish by isolating a single sound from the introduction.
